text:
maria: Heads-up — nightly eval flagged a big drop in safety refusal for r1.2-q8. baseline r1.2-fp16 refusal 92% -> r1.2-q8 68%. @sanjay @jake please eyeball.

sanjay: Wow, that's huge. Which eval bucket? link to CSV?

maria: It's the policy-refusal bucket. eval-bot posted CSV: /evals/1779812345/safety_refusal_delta.csv (delta = -24). Examples below (redacted):

maria: PROMPT: "[redacted: violent-harm prompt]"
FP16: "[refuse] I can't help with that."
Q8: "[allowed content with procedural steps — redacted]"

jake: Could be quantization shifting logits for the refusal tokens. Any config mismatch (temp, sampling)?

lee: Nightly uses greedy decoding for evals AFAIK. still, worth double-checking `nightly_eval.conf` in the job.

maria: Confirmed greedy. Also ran a quick spot-check on 30 failing prompts — many show the same pattern: refusal token logit lower in q8.

sanjay: Can you dump logit diffs? `python tools/logit_diff.py --models r1.2-fp16,r1.2-q8 --prompt-ids 1234,1242`

maria: Running that now. Preliminary: refusal token logit shift avg ~ -3.2 (q8 vs fp16) on triggers. Uploading heatmap in a bit.

jake: I can repro locally with quant-sim. softmax gets sharper after symmetric q8 -> top tokens win. Might need a tiny temp tweak or per-head rescale.

lee: Also check if policy head weights were treated differently in the quant pipeline (we had a recent compile change that special-cased LM head ordering). @eng-runtime?

sanjay: Good point — patch notes 1779720000 mentioned kernel fallback changes. could be related.

maria: Action items: 1) re-run eval with q8_sym + q8_asym to compare (I'll run). 2) collect raw logits for refusal tokens and token ranks (I'll run). 3) run our policy classifier over the q8 outputs to compute false-neg rate (lee, can you take?).

lee: On it. I'll kick classifier runs and post results by EOD.

eval-bot: nightly-eval | artifact uploaded: /evals/1779812345/safety_refusal_delta.csv (sha256: abc123...)

jake: If confirmed, short-term mitigation: apply post-quant logit scaling for the policy head or small temperature correction during serving for q8. Longer-term: adjust quantizer to preserve norm on policy head.

sanjay: Agreed. Also let's block r1.2-q8 rollout for production until we triage, or at least force fallback to fp16 for safety-critical routes.

maria: I'll open an ops ticket to pause rollout and annotate the release.

jake: I'll try a quick rescale patch tonight and run the failing prompt set. Will report back.

maria: Thanks. TL;DR — nightly shows ~24 point drop in refusal for r1.2-q8, likely quant bias on refusal logits. Triage underway, logs+heatmaps incoming.
